correctness.rationale: Exact proof: coordinatewise partial bijections of occupied first and second coordinates give a permanent k-pebble response when each axis size agrees after truncation at k; at most \(k-1\) positions are occupied before a move. Clique and independent-set maxima are \(\max(a,b)\) and \(\min(a,b)\), witnessed and separated by formulas with at most k variable names. \(\mathrm{FO}^{2}\) collapses because every vertex has an adjacent and a nonadjacent distinct vertex. Isomorphism and canonical size then follow from the two exact extrema. Independent programs checked 236 finite logical comparisons plus 68,272 post-pruning subset candidates for small cases. Finite checks are supporting evidence and not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Rook graphs are standard line graphs of complete bipartite graphs, two-factor Cartesian products, and natural structures in Hamming/Johnson graph model theory. Their exact unrestricted counting-free bounded-variable classification is a complete structural problem, giving a two-variable collapse, a sharp threshold formula, exactly \(\binom{k}{2}\) theories, unique minimum representatives of bounded order \(k^2\), and strict variable hierarchy. These are motivated family-wide statements, not merely a small enumeration or renaming of the source-graph result.
